correctness.rationale: Radial Toeplitz diagonalization yields exact gamma-density integrals. The adjacent difference is a signed four-exponential polynomial with no more than three zeros; outside the two annuli the difference has fixed sign. Stirling/Edgeworth expansion uniformly with derivatives at index n=T+s sqrt(T) gives symmetric Gaussian mixture G_delta and first odd correction J_delta. The derivative roots of G_delta are one for 0<delta<1, three for delta>1 with a unique positive r satisfying r=delta tanh(delta r). Zero counting upgrades local root persistence to global modal-count classification. Evaluating J_delta(±r) yields positive inward-vs-outward height gap C_delta/T+O(T^-3/2); optimizing the primary peak gives stated norm. Independent gamma-integral sampling at T=5000, delta=.6 and 1.5 confirms one and two maxima and inward dominance; finite sampling does not establish large-T quantifiers.

evidence: Dewage--Ólafsson Theorem 2.12 and Proposition 6.2 give radial spectra and spectral-algebra density; Knutsen gives radial-Cantor one-ring operator estimates.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General diagonalization is prior; it does not specify the discrete two-annulus peak competition or first asymmetry coefficient.
